Here’s the fastest way to handle this on a big US bank with an iOS app, plus exact wording you can use.

1) Use the iOS app right now  
On your iPhone:
1. Open your bank’s app.  
2. Log in → go to **Accounts**.  
3. Find and tap your **Credit Card** (it will usually be listed separately from Checking/Debit).  
4. On the credit card screen, look for one of:
   - **“Manage card”** or **“Card controls”**  
   - **“Report lost/stolen”**  
   - A small **card icon** or **three dots (…)** menu in the top corner
5. Tap **Report lost or stolen** (or similar).  
6. Choose **Stolen** (not “Misplaced” or “Temporarily lock”).  
7. Confirm you want:
   - The current card **permanently blocked**, and  
   - A **replacement card issued**.

If you don’t see that option:
- Go to **Menu** (≡) → **Help & Support** or **Customer Service** → **Message Center** or **Chat**.

2) If you can call (do this in parallel if possible)  
From the app or website, open **Help / Contact us** and tap the **24/7 Credit Card / Lost or Stolen Card** number.

When they answer, say this clearly:

> “My credit card has been **stolen from my wallet**. It is not misplaced. I need you to **block it immediately and issue a replacement card**. I also need you to **review recent transactions and flag anything that looks unauthorized**.”

If they ask what you need, be specific:
- “Please **cancel and permanently block** the current credit card number.”  
- “Please **issue a new card** and tell me the **estimated delivery date**.”  
- “Please **review today’s and recent transactions** and open a **fraud case** for any charges I don’t recognize.”

3) If you use secure in‑app messaging or chat  
You can copy‑paste and send this in the app’s message center/chat:

> “My credit card has been **stolen from my wallet** (not misplaced). I need you to **immediately block the card and issue a replacement**. Please also **review recent transactions** and let me know how to dispute any unauthorized charges.”

4) Right after it’s blocked  
Ask the bank’s agent (or confirm in chat):
- Is the **card number changing**? (Usually yes.)  
- **When** will the replacement arrive?  
- Will any **scheduled or recurring payments** be affected?

Write down:
- Date and **time** of the report  
- Any **case / reference number**  
- The **representative’s name or ID**, if given  

5) Next couple of days  
- Watch your checking and credit card activity for anything unfamiliar.  
- Once the new card arrives, **update subscriptions and billers** that charged the old card.

If you tell me your bank’s name (e.g., Chase, Bank of America, etc.), I can give you much more exact tap-by-tap instructions specific to that app.</action>
